How to use the Compound Interest Calculator

  1. Enter your starting amount and how much you plan to add each month.
  2. Set the expected annual return and the number of years.
  3. Pick how often interest compounds. Results update instantly.
  4. Scroll the table to see your balance at the end of each year.

Frequently asked questions

What is compound interest?

Compound interest is interest earned on both your original money and on the interest it has already earned. Over long periods this snowball effect makes growth accelerate.

What rate of return should I use?

High-yield savings accounts may pay 3–5% per year. Broad stock market index funds have historically averaged around 7% per year after inflation, but returns vary and are not guaranteed.

Does compounding frequency matter much?

Slightly. More frequent compounding earns a bit more, but the difference between monthly and daily is small. The rate, the time horizon and your contributions matter far more.

Is this financial advice?

No. This calculator is for educational estimates only and does not account for taxes, fees or inflation.
